name: Dutasteride

lead: Dutasteride (Avodart) is an inhibitor of both type I and type II 5-alpha-reductase, approved for benign prostatic hyperplasia. It is used off-label, and approved for male pattern hair loss in South Korea and Japan, as a stronger alternative to finasteride.

Head-to-head and pooled analyses indicate that dutasteride produces larger increases in hair counts than 1 mg finasteride, particularly at 0.5 mg, though the comparative trial evidence is limited and sexual side effect comparisons are not conclusive.

paras: By blocking all active 5-alpha-reductase isoenzymes, dutasteride suppresses serum DHT by more than 90 percent, versus around 70 percent for finasteride. Since scalp follicles express type I as well as type II enzyme, this broader blockade is thought to protect more follicles from DHT-driven miniaturisation.

Reported adverse effects resemble those of finasteride: reduced libido, erectile and ejaculatory problems, and mood effects in some users. Its very long half-life means effects can persist for weeks after stopping. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and affects PSA, and it is prescription-only. For hair loss it is largely an off-label use in Western markets.
